details: clampony copies the npm package clamp (its index.js, test and README) and adds a `preinstall` hook, `node setup.js`, that runs on npm install. In versions 1.0.9 to 1.0.11, setup.js downloads a next stage from `https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J`, with `https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw` as a fallback; in these versions the step that would write the download to disk and run it is still an empty function. Both URLs serve the same obfuscated Windows stealer that copies Telegram Desktop session data, SSH keys, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, npm, PyPI, Git and GitHub CLI credentials, FileZilla, WinSCP and MobaXterm sessions and shell histories, zips them and uploads the archive to a Telegram bot through a list of HTTP proxies, and also downloads and runs `https://195.123.6.29:443/enterotoxin.exe`. The npm account tinafo6772 published seven versions of clampony within 20 minutes on 2026-11-24, adding the downloader step by step.
